chronic hyperthyroid state in hamster model is associated with normal or enhanced intrinsic myocyte function but with impaired global cardiac function.
chronic hyperthyroid state is associated with normal or enhanced intrinsic cardiac myocyte function despite decline in global cardiac function.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic hyperthyroid-induced LV remodeling and dysfunction are associated with normal or enhanced intrinsic LV myocyte function.
chronic hyperthyroid state in the F1b hamster leads to LV chamber remodeling and dysfunction, and this is accompanied by myocyte hypertrophy and enhanced intrinsic contractile performance.
chronic hyperthyroid hamster hearts are characterized by significant LV remodeling and impaired global cardiac function, but enhanced myocyte contractile function, and increased LV collagen content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic hyperthyroid states are detrimental to LV structure and function.
chronic hyperthyroid state can lead to cardiac remodeling and global cardiac dysfunction, but the underlying mechanism is likely multifactorial.

chronic hyperthyroid state may be associated with a decline in global cardiac function, at least partly due to increased interstitial fibrosis, in the face of normal or enhanced individual cardiomyocyte function.
